subject: dietary fiber and gut bacteria
title: What If You Never Ate Fiber Again?

scenes.text: What if you never ate fiber again? Your gut bacteria wouldn't go hungry for long.
Most people already eat only about fourteen grams a day, half the roughly twenty-eight recommended. Ninety-five percent fall short.
You can't digest fiber yourself. It travels to your colon, where trillions of bacteria live on it.
In mice fed zero fiber, within just a few days some of those bacteria switched to a new meal: the mucus lining the gut.
That protective layer turned thin and patchy. When a gut infection arrived, the fiber-starved mice got far sicker.
As one of the researchers put it: if you don't feed them, they can eat you.
